findings.statement: The deny leg proves only the RESOLVER decision; a second public read entry point still serves the denied root's bytes. In a catalog whose fifth root declares reusable_for_filing: false, SourceResolver.resolve(exact) correctly returns missing, yet the same catalog's SourceResolver.read_verified_bytes(handle) returns ok=True / status='verified' with the real 59 bytes of the denied document, because that entry point enforces only root containment (resolver.py:2022 _inside_configured_roots) and never consults reusable_root_ids. The harness never exercises that path, so the L04 sub-clause '不以平权绕过能力限制' is evidenced for one of the two read entry points only. The catalog layer's own docstring (resolver.py:1958-1963) scopes the primitive to 'callers that ask this resolver for bytes' and declares the direct-canonical_path bypass out of its scope, and consumer-side containment (filing-fetch validate_handle + policy_snapshot.path_ref) is a separate gate — so this is a coverage/over-claim gap, not a broken deny.
findings.evidence: Reviewer probe (temp-only, %TEMP%\reviewer-r3\probe_deny_read_bypass.py, run with PYTHONPATH=company-wiki/src): 'deny scan exit: 0 ... target role/status/size: original_primary active 59 ... resolve status: missing ... read_verified_bytes on the DENIED root: ok=True status=verified byte_size=59 bytes_source=handle sha256=e34a69ef... data sha256=e34a69ef... data is the file on disk: True'. The handle was built from the deny catalog's own locations row (landed under the deny catalog's configured fifth root, so containment passes). Supporting code: run_bar_fifth_root_isolated.py:459-477 (read_verified) is only ever called on the POSITIVE catalog; the deny leg (lines 913-929) records resolve + query_filing_candidates only. The prose states the narrow fact correctly (evidence/b-ar-fifth-root-isolated.md:68-70, 130-131), but the L04 mapping table's last row asserts '不以平权绕过能力限制' on the strength of the policy export.
findings.why_it_matters: L04's second half is the increment's stated acceptance target, and 'deny' is a capability limit at the root level. A reader of the record may conclude that reusable_for_filing: false blocks access to the root, whereas it blocks exactly one decision (reuse-by-such-a-name) while the byte primitive will still hand over the bytes to any caller holding a handle, and query_filing_candidates(root_ids=...) will still list the same 2 rows including absolute_path. The record should either exercise read_verified_bytes against the deny catalog and report the result, or state plainly that the deny is a resolver-scoped decision and that the byte primitive is not gated by reusable_for_filing.
